metadata.formula: PPR_tC = catch_t * saved classic wet-weight-equivalent SPPR / 9; if coefficient absent but saved TL present, TE**(1-TL); divide by 9 exactly once. Recorded zero catch gives zero contribution even with missing coefficient.
metadata.group_name_policy: Exact native strings and source seq IDs; display labels strip only trailing whitespace.
metadata.source_branch: Native detailed supplement Table A, 39 stock nodes; 2 fishery nodes omitted from Ecopath stock calculation. Source prose/supplement Sardine landings conflict preserved.
metadata.allocation_basis: Source native artisanal+commercial LANDINGS first to match reference2019 landings, then complete BIOMASS when all candidate landings total zero; fixed map reused all years/bases as stated assumption.
metadata.membership_allocation_combination: Weaker required component; High > Medium > Low > Very low > Unresolved.
metadata.authorization_boundary: Candidate mapping/calculations only; no active workbook selection, adoption, Project/atlas or researcher signoff changes.
metadata.search_coverage: Bounded primary/authoritative searches retained in search_records.json and raw search batches. Failed full texts are identified; no snippet or gear/legal/mean-size summary is treated as measured caught-mass allocation.

sources.title: Primary composition searches, decisions and bounded access failures
sources.supports: Actual final query strings and provider outputs; applicable observed composition not established, so modeled proxy allocations remain explicitly assumed.

sources.title: Chiaverano et al. (2018), Northern Humboldt ecological network
sources.supports: Focal inheritance, domain/period, added jellyfish/turtles/eggs, source-version qualifications; DOI 10.1016/j.pocean.2018.04.009.

sources.title: Original revised/final supplement, Table A: resolved stock parameters and fleet removals
sources.supports: Exact stock IDs/names, stored biomass C and fleet landings I/J and discards K/L; all zeros are explicit. Native supplement landings are used as composition proxies.

sources.title: Independent fresh group definitions and evidence scopes
sources.supports: Exact stock definitions; inherited enumerated examples distinguished from parameter analogues and unsupported exhaustive lists.

sources.title: Independent source catch and biomass vector with exact cell locators
sources.supports: Every candidate raw value and genuine zero, source basis and fallback inputs.

sources.title: Tam et al. (2008), inherited Northern Humboldt model methods, pp.353–354
sources.supports: Explicit species examples, three Peruvian hake intervals, plankton size classes; parameter analogues are not source-membership observations.

sources.title: LME 013 regional Catch, Classic PPR and NPP tables, read-only snapshot
sources.supports: All exact reporting labels and functional/common names, all bases/years, saved independent classic TL/SPPR and NPP. Active selection was not changed.

sources.title: Sea Around Us, catch reconstruction and allocation methods
sources.supports: Commercial/functional reporting groups differ from taxa and maximum size is not caught-size mass composition; page opened 2026-10-03.

sources.title: WoRMS/FishBase/MolluscaBase authority records retained from 30 September 2026
sources.supports: Taxonomic identity, accepted name, family/order, marine/freshwater status and authority IDs for all available exact catch names. These records are reused taxonomy evidence, not prior mapping assignments.

sources.title: WoRMS Merlucciidae taxonomic list and accepted Peruvian hake identity
sources.supports: Merluccius gayi peruanus accepted as M. peruanus; M. gayi and M. australis retained distinct. Search result read; full endpoint fetch failed 2026-10-03.

sources.title: OBIS, Loligo gahi taxon entry
sources.supports: Accepted Doryteuthis gahi identity for source Loligo gahi; full entry opened 2026-10-03.

sources.title: IMARPE 2019 Scientific and Technical Yearbook, p.38, hake fishery size structure
sources.supports: Primary indexed passage describes industrial catch lengths, not matching all-region caught-mass bins for exact model intervals. Full PDF retrieval failed; no fractions adopted.

sources.title: IMARPE 2016 Vol.43 No.2, p.158, coastal fishery species and caught lengths
sources.supports: Regional small sciaenids and historical family nomenclature; primary indexed table only. A single coastal fishery does not supply whole-LME residual-label proportions.

sources.title: IMARPE 1995–1996 commercial species list and later demersal records
sources.supports: Primary indexed commercial list names Congrio = Genypterus maculatus; later records distinguish Ophichthus anguila. Supports generic-pool interpretation, not focal explicit membership.

sources.title: IMARPE 2025 pelagic survey, p.34, Grimothea monodon in midwater catch
sources.supports: Primary indexed pelagic occurrence and meaningful squat-lobster analogue; survey catches do not determine broad regional commercial residual composition.

sources.title: IMARPE public fishery activity reporting service and 2013 marine invertebrate landings
sources.supports: Regional fisheries report scallop/snail/octopus/squid/crab resources separately; national totals do not establish catch composition of unidentified SAU labels.

sources.title: FAO shark habitat/species catalogue and Galeorhinus fishery review
sources.supports: Mixed demersal/pelagic Galeorhinus ecology; primary FAO catalogue and regional records inform elasmobranch guilds. No compatible regional observed habitat-pool catch fractions were adopted.

sources.title: FishBase orange roughy species summary
sources.supports: Deep bathypelagic habitat (typically 400–900m) differs from the represented coastal guild; indexed primary authority page read 2026-10-03.

sources.title: NIWA, new science on inanga
sources.supports: Marine larvae and freshwater adult life establish a true life-history mismatch, rather than following the inconsistent provider large-reef tag.

very_low_decision_groups.reason: Broad fish reporting labels have unknown composition across named and residual pools, historical taxonomic scope, and potentially unrepresented deep-water members; native landings approximate their mixtures.
Broad/historical cartilaginous labels cross benthic and water-column pools with unrepresented chimaera or filter-feeding ray components.
Benthic chimaera assigned to a benthic elasmobranch analogue despite belonging to Holocephali rather than Elasmobranchii.
Broad crustacean reporting mixes benthic and pelagic components; a macrozooplankton/benthos approximation uses biomass because both native landings are zero, with a 2–20 mm size mismatch.
Large deep-water colder-water fishes use the closest medium-demersal analogue; source population, depth and size mismatch remain.
Pelagic/benthic squat-lobster catch lacks a separate source population; macrozooplankton/benthos analogues and biomass weights retain the 2–20 mm mismatch.
Amphidromous galaxiid lacks a corresponding source population; a coastal small-fish analogue is assumed.
Non-Peruvian hake/cod-like fishes use Peruvian hake groups; species, southern ecology and size boundaries differ, and native stage landings are transferred.
Pelagic filter-feeding manta uses the closest chondrichthyan pool despite the source apex-predator correspondence.
Snake eel mapped to unnamed conger pool despite taxonomic identity differing from the regional congrio interpretation.
